title: The Authority Firewall: A Machine-Checked Separation of Evidence from Authority in Finite Systems
description: A finite verifier's certificate type splits as a coproduct T = T_auth + (T_res + F_res) — authority terminals in one summand, all residual/defect outcomes in the other. We establish, axiom-free in Lean 4, that no residual outcome inhabits the authority summand; within this terminal-type discipline, residual evidence cannot directly be interpreted as an authority terminal. In a finite verification system structured around a two-lane architecture — an evidence lane for obstruction diagnostics and a separate lane for authority certification — the evidence lane and the authority lane are structurally disjoint: a residual outcome classified by the evidence lane cannot be read as an authority terminal through the residual terminalizer. Any authority promotion must pass through a separately declared authority route. The pointwise form of this Separation Theorem is verified axiom-free in Lean 4 without custom axioms. The categorical formulation (Nat(Omega_LambdaOmega, Auth) = empty) is formulated as an open conditional upon a prose reduction. We illustrate the firewall via an adversarial review of a solver whose authority gate refused promotion. This monograph assigns no authorization and changes no jurisdiction. It carries no operational authority or institutional standing.
